items.stem: A batch rendering job can be safely interrupted and restarted. Which Compute Engine option minimizes cost for it?

options.rationale: Correct: spot VMs are cheapest and acceptable when the workload tolerates preemption.
On-demand costs more and is unnecessary for an interruptible job.

options.text: A 3-year committed use for on-demand VMs
options.rationale: Commitments suit steady baseline load, not a one-off batch job.
Sole-tenant nodes add cost for isolation the job does not need.

items.explanation: Correct: spot VMs are the cheapest option for interruptible, restartable workloads.

items.stem: Which TWO settings help keep SSH access to a VM secure? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Restrict the SSH firewall rule to known source IP ranges
options.rationale: Correct: limiting source ranges reduces the attack surface.

options.text: Use OS Login with IAM-managed SSH keys
options.rationale: Correct: OS Login centralizes key management under IAM.
Opening SSH to the world exposes the VM to broad attack.

options.text: Embed a shared private key in the boot image
options.rationale: Baking a shared key into an image is a serious credential-leak risk.

items.explanation: Correct: restricting source ranges and using OS Login both tighten SSH access.

items.stem: You need a VM that automatically recovers capacity if an instance fails and scales with load. What should you use?

options.text: A managed instance group with autoscaling and health checks
options.rationale: Correct: a MIG recreates failed instances and scales on a metric.
A standalone VM has no self-healing or scaling.
Unmanaged groups do not autoscale or auto-heal.
A bucket stores objects and does not run compute.

items.explanation: Correct: a managed instance group provides auto-healing and autoscaling.
